title: mcpmoat scan output
description: The JSON document that `mcpmoat scan --json` writes to stdout. The document never holds env or header values. A finding names the key it is about, never the value. Text fields that come from servers or config files are untrusted: non-printable and invisible non-ASCII characters are written as \uXXXX escapes. Long names and paths are cut, and then "fields_truncated" is true. Every enum lists all the values that mcpmoat writes.

schema_version.description: Version of this output format. It is 3 for this schema.

mode.description: How the scan ran. "no-connect" only reads configs. "connect" also connects to the servers.

complete.description: False when the report can miss results: a config file has a problem (see "errors"), or the inspection or the pin step failed as a whole (for example, pins.json cannot be read), or the LLM step of a --llm scan did not classify every tool: a provider failure, an internal error of the LLM step, or more tools than the --llm cap. The exit code is then 2, and the reason is on stderr. A failed save of new pins comes after the document is written, so "complete" can be true while the exit code is 2. Always check the exit code too.

fields_truncated.description: True when at least one text field was cut at its length cap. A cut value ends with "..." and holds at most 515 characters (a name) or 4099 characters (a path). Each cut field has a maxLength in this schema. The diff text, argv, url, command and digest are never cut.

servers.description: Every server that the scan found. Empty list when there is none.

findings.description: Every finding that is not ignored. Empty list when there is none.

diffs.description: One diff for each tool that differs from the pins. Empty list when there is none.

errors.description: Config problems that the scan found. Empty list when there is none.

ignored.description: How many findings an ignore entry (.mcpmoat-ignore or --ignore) dropped from "findings". Always present, with zero counts when nothing was ignored.

total.description: Number of findings that were dropped. It is the sum of the counts in "rules".

rules.description: Number of dropped findings for each rule. The keys are rule IDs only, never text from the ignore file. Empty object when nothing was ignored.

file_entries.description: Number of entries that mcpmoat read from .mcpmoat-ignore (the N in the stderr line 'using N entries'). Some of them may not apply to any finding.

accept.description: The hint that tells how to accept the changes of a server. It holds what the terminal hint shows.

digest.description: The pin digest that the terminal hint shows: "pd1:" and 64 lowercase hex digits. It is never cut.

command.description: The command that the terminal hint shows. Present only when the terminal hint prints a command, never when it prints prose steps. It is never cut.

tool.description: The program that made the report.

server.description: One MCP server from a client config. The document has no env, no header and no working directory.

name.description: Server name from the config. Untrusted text.

client.description: The client whose config declares the server.

scope.description: "global" for a user-wide config. "project" for a server of one project.

project_path.description: Path of the project for a project server. Empty string means none. Untrusted text.

untrusted.description: True for a server from a project file, which a cloned repository can ship.

state.description: Whether the client config turns the server on. "project-approved" means that only files from the repository approved the server.

transport.description: How mcpmoat talks to the server.

source.description: Path of the config file that declares the server. Untrusted text. Not the origin of a finding: that is findings[].source.

argv.description: Command line of a stdio server. It is redacted: secret-looking values are masked. Absent for http and sse servers.

url.description: URL of an http or sse server. It is redacted: credentials and secret-looking parts are masked. Absent for stdio servers.

accept.description: How to accept the changes of this server. Absent when the server has nothing to accept.

inspection.description: What happened when mcpmoat inspected the server.

status.description: "not_run": mcpmoat did not connect. This happens in no-connect mode. It also happens in connect mode when the inspection or the pin step fails as a whole (for example, pins.json cannot be read): then every server is "not_run", the exit code is 2 and the reason is on stderr. "ok": it connected and listed the tools. "timeout": the server did not answer in time. "failed": the connection or the tool list failed. "refused": mcpmoat chose not to connect, for example to a disabled or untrusted server. Two servers with the same client, source, project_path and name share one status: "ok" when one of them was inspected.

finding.description: One finding. For every string field except "source", an empty string means that the field does not apply.

rule_id.description: ID of the rule that matched, for example MOAT-T2-004.

severity.description: Severity word of the rule. Known values are "low", "medium", "high" and "critical". This is a plain string, not an enum, because the Go code accepts any string here and treats an unknown value as failing. Consumers must handle other values.

server.description: Name of the server that the finding is about. Untrusted text. Empty string means none.

field.description: Config field that matched, for example "env" or "args". Empty string means none.

key.description: Key name in the field, for example an env variable name. Only keys, never values. Untrusted text. Empty string means none.

related.description: A second name that the finding refers to, for example a second server, a fixed reason text, or, for MOAT-LLM-001, the category of the verdict. Untrusted text. Empty string means none.

source.description: What made the finding (not the config file of a server: that is servers[].source). "rule": a finding from a mcpmoat rule (a built-in check or a rule file), not from the LLM. "llm": the optional LLM classification (--llm) made it. An "llm" finding is advisory: a model made it, not a rule.

diff.description: The diff of one tool against its pin.

server.description: Name of the server. Untrusted text.

tool.description: Name of the tool. Untrusted text.

kind.description: "changed": the pinned and the current text differ. "new": the server offers a tool that the pins do not hold. "unverified": a pinned tool whose pin cannot be checked.

diff.description: Unified diff as raw server text, or a fixed note of mcpmoat when "diff_is_note" is true. It is untrusted. JSON escaping covers control characters, and non-printable or invisible non-ASCII characters are written as \uXXXX escapes. Do not write it to a terminal without care.

diff_truncated.description: True when the stored diff was cut, so "diff" is not the whole diff.

diff_is_note.description: True when "diff" is a fixed note, not a unified diff: the diff could not be made, or the change does not show in the rendered text.

fileError.description: One config problem. The text of the underlying error is never included.

path.description: Path of the config file. Untrusted text.

project_path.description: Path of the project for a project config. Empty string means none. Untrusted text.

server.description: Name of the server that the problem is about. Empty string means a problem with the whole file. Untrusted text.

line.description: 1-based line of the problem. 0 means unknown.

col.description: 1-based byte column of the problem. 0 means unknown.

reason.description: Fixed text that tells what is wrong.

untrusted.description: True when the problem is in a project file, which a cloned repository can ship.
